--- title: "Vocabulary: multiple choice" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · L_ORAL_SEM_VOCABULARIO_OPCIONES" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class B). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea L_ORAL_SEM_VOCABULARIO_OPCIONES`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Vocabulario: elección entre opciones*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/L_ORAL_SEM_VOCABULARIO_OPCIONES.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class B.** It has enough data to be described, but it lacks some of the guarantees of class A (stability across time points, item-level reliability or validity). Use with caution and not for individual decisions. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Vocabulary: multiple choice, from age 4 to 6 (5,220 administrations in 6 cohorts). Stability across time points ρ = .13. AUC .53–.58 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 124 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | reading and picture selection | | Items | 17 | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The child selects among four options the picture corresponding to the word given by the experimenter. | ## Theoretical framework These tasks measure **receptive oral language**. In listening comprehension, the child hears a text without seeing it and answers questions by choosing among options. In multiple-choice vocabulary, the child hears a word and chooses among four pictures. In the simple view of reading, listening comprehension is the component that does not depend on reading [@hoover1990simple]. The vocabulary framework covers expressive and reading vocabulary. **What the evidence says:** - **In transparent orthographies, listening comprehension is the best predictor of reading comprehension.** In 1,895 Italian children from Grade 1 to Grade 5, listening comprehension predicted reading comprehension in every grade and reading accuracy played a smaller role [@tobia2015simple]. In 1,815 Finnish children, the effect of fluency disappeared after Grade 1 and that of listening comprehension remained until Grade 3 [@torppa2016simple]. In 4,750 Dominican schoolchildren, its weight grows as reading comprehension improves [@sanchezvincitore2022svr]. - **Preschool oral language anticipates reading comprehension.** In children aged 4 to 6, inferences, literal comprehension of a story and grammar predicted reading comprehension a year later; vocabulary acted through them [@silva2014comprehension]. Language in a broad sense predicts more than vocabulary alone [@lervag2018comprehension]. - **Receptive vocabulary predicts level, not rate.** In two Australian samples (N = 4,983 and 4,570), receptive vocabulary at age 4 predicted comprehension at age 8, but its growth was not related to reading growth between ages 8 and 14 [@larsen2026receptive]. The relation is weak in the first grades, when decoding limits comprehension, and grows later. These tasks can be expected to predict little in the short term. **What our data show.** They are the weakest tasks in their domain: - **Low consistency.** Listening comprehension has α = .30 with 10 items; multiple-choice vocabulary, α = .51. The latter is also very unstable across terms (ρ = .12–.14) and its observed maximum (25) exceeds the number of items (17), which needs to be reviewed. - **Low predictive validity.** Against low reading comprehension at ages 7 and 8, the AUC is .58–.59 for listening comprehension and .52–.58 for vocabulary. They are not suitable for individual decisions. Before using them in articles, the items and scoring should be reviewed. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.1| 2012| 154|2016/17 | 385| 385| 0| 17| | 4.1| 2013| 181|2017/18 | 577| 569| 8| 24| | 4.1| 2015| 894|2019/20 | 493| 0| 493| 22| | 5.1| 2011| 153|2016/17 | 879| 0| 879| 34| | 5.1| 2012| 182|2017/18 | 320| 316| 0| 16| | 5.1| 2014| 896|2019/20 | 349| 13| 336| 21| | 6.1| 2010| 152|2016/17 | 870| 244| 625| 34| | 6.1| 2011| 183|2017/18 | 779| 0| 779| 31| | 6.1| 2013| 898|2019/20 | 568| 398| 170| 35| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|----------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 4.1| 954| 2012, 2013| 6.26| 2.45| 6| 0.52| 0.63| 0.00| | 5.1| 329| 2012, 2014| 7.09| 2.28| 7| -0.14| 0.00| 0.00| | 6.1| 642| 2010, 2013| 8.17| 2.44| 8| 0.53| 0.00| 1.09| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). Internal consistency in the 2021 analyses: α = .51. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2011| 5.1| 6.1| 690| 0.09| 0.13| | 2012| 4.1| 5.1| 305| 0.15| 0.12| | 2013| 4.1| 6.1| 320| 0.15| 0.14| ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Vocabulary and oral comprehension (4.1, r = .34); Letter knowledge (5.1, r = .20); Vocabulary and oral comprehension (6.1, r = .21). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .53–.58. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .52–.58. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_SEM_VOCABULARIO_OPCIONES_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .56–.62 (3 time points; 214–678 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|----------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4.1| 954| 2012, 2013| 3| 3| 4| 5| 6| 8| 9| | 5.1| 329| 2012, 2014| 3| 4| 5| 6| 7| 9| 10| | 6.1| 642| 2010, 2013| 4| 5| 6| 7| 8| 9| 11| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_SEM_VOCABULARIO_OPCIONES_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.1| 1,188| 0.090| 0.002| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.1| 1,453| 0.116| 0.027| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.1| 1,450| 0.086| 0.001| |School (ICC) | 4.1| 1,455| 0.048| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.1| 1,473| 0.023| 0.379| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.1| 1,513| 0.140| 0.006| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.1| 1,521| 0.043| 0.092| |School (ICC) | 5.1| 1,548| 0.064| | |School SES (ρ) | 6.1| 2,204| 0.092| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.1| 2,210| 0.062| 0.143| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.1| 2,207| 0.003| 0.905| |School (ICC) | 6.1| 2,217| 0.050| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Vocabulary: multiple choice” (code 124; LEEDUCA battery) assesses receptive vocabulary. The child reads the written stimulus on the screen and selects the matching picture. It comprises 17 items. The time limit is 120 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014 and 2015 cohorts it was administered in 9 sessions, from 4 to 6 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .51 (N = 4,599, 17 items). Stability across time points was ρ = .12–.14. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .52–.58. ## Pending issues - Estabilidad muy baja entre aplicaciones (ρ = .14): revisar los datos (códigos, versiones o tiempos) antes de usar la tarea *(Spanish)* - La puntuación máxima observada (25) supera el número de ítems (17): puede que se puntúen los ítems de ejemplo, que haya una versión con más ítems o un error de datos. Comprobar antes de describir la tarea y distinguir ítems de prueba y de ejemplo. *(Spanish)* - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
